canvas-01-1.description: The lower left quarter of the title sheet of the Allentown atlas, set off from the key map and index by a heavy rule, shows a block of the village of Crosswicks, in Chesterfield Township, Burlington County, under the heading At Crosswicks. Ward Avenue crosses the part from west to east and Buttonwood runs down its eastern edge, with the head of Front Street meeting Buttonwood at the bottom. The block numbers 28 and 29 cover open lots with scattered frame dwellings, coops, sheds, auto garages and corn cribs. North of Ward Avenue stand the Episcopal church with its rectory and the Orthodox Quaker meeting house, drawn in pink as brick and heated by hot air with kerosene lamps. Four-inch water pipes are drawn along Ward Avenue and Buttonwood, with a fire hydrant at the corner, and the western edge is marked No Exposure. The part adjoins sheet 2, which draws Buttonwood and the centre of the village, and sheet 3 to the north; the match numbers 2 and 3 appear on its edges. Its own scale bar and north arrow are drawn inside it, and the arrow points almost straight up the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Placed from two hand-picked junctions on Buttonwood (Ward Avenue and Front Street); the fit is a helmert along one street, so rotation rests on that street alone.
Buttonwood is Buttonwood Street in OpenStreetMap; south of Front Street it is Bordentown-Crosswicks Road.

Sheet 1: title, key map of Allentown, Crosswicks, Nelsonville and Imlaystown (1110 ft to an inch), water and fire notes, legend and index; the lower left quarter is a 100 ft map of Crosswicks (Ward Av. and Buttonwood), configured as part 1.

sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the centre of the village of Crosswicks, Chesterfield Township, Burlington County. North Main comes down from the north-west to Ward Avenue, Church runs south from Ward Avenue to Front, and Main runs east from Church past the junction with New, crossing Chesterfield Road at the Crosswicks Hotel and continuing east past the cemetery. Buttonwood bounds the sheet on the west and Chesterfield Road runs south on the east. Bricks Alley joins Main and Front between Church and Chesterfield Road. The sheet shows the Methodist Episcopal church, the Hicksite Quaker meeting house, the public school, the fire department, the post office, the Crosswicks Hotel, an A.M.E. church, C. D. Anderson's garage, T. B. Anderson's lumber sheds, Edgar Brick and Sons' mince meat factory with its packing and shipping house, and Charles W. Brick's chicken farm with long chicken houses and brooder houses filling the large block 24 in the south. Water pipes of four and six inches with hydrants run along the main streets. A dash-dot match line marked A and B at the top joins sheet 3, and sheet 1 adjoins on the west. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: North Main is today part of Church Street; Chesterfield Road is Chesterfield-Crosswicks Road; Buttonwood is Buttonwood Street.
New Street now meets Main Street at the Chesterfield-Crosswicks Road junction in OpenStreetMap; the sheet draws it joining Chesterfield Road about 250 ft north of Main.
Crosswicks centre: N. Main, Ward Av., Church, Main, New, Front, Buttonwood, Chesterfield Rd, Bricks Alley. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the north end of Crosswicks, Chesterfield Township, Burlington County. North Main runs from the steel bridge over Crosswicks Creek at the bottom up to a four-way junction with Trenton Road from the north-west, Newtown Road to the north and Maple to the east. Brick runs parallel to North Main on the west from Trenton Road down to Charles W. Brick's grist mill, electric light and ice plant on the creek, which is drawn with its dam, wheel house and a note on its sprinklers and water supply. Oak, marked arbitrary, crosses between Brick and North Main, Maple is likewise marked arbitrary, and Allentown Road leaves North Main towards the south-east. Most of the sheet is open land in large numbered blocks with scattered dwellings, coops, chicken houses and an auto repair shop with a buried gasoline tank near the main junction. Crosswicks Creek and its millpond loop cover the lower left of the sheet. A dash-dot match line marked A and B at the bottom joins sheet 2, and the number 1 marks where sheet 1 adjoins. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Modern names: North Main is Church Street; Trenton Road and Maple are South Broad Street; Newtown Road is Crosswicks-Hamilton Square Road; Brick is Mill Road; Oak is Cross Street; Allentown Road is Old York Road.
Maple and Oak are printed with the word Arbitrary, meaning their house numbers are arbitrary.
Crosswicks north: N. Main, Trenton Rd, Newtown Rd, Maple, Brick, Oak, Allentown Rd, Crosswicks Creek, Brick's grist mill. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-4-1.description: The main part of sheet 4 covers the south-western end of the borough of Allentown, Monmouth County. Main runs up the sheet from Yardville Road at the bottom to the steel bridge over Doctors Creek at the top, where Conine's Millpond spreads east of the bridge. High leaves Main to the north-east past the cemetery and the First Presbyterian Church of Allentown with its parish house. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Frame dwellings with stables, auto garages and coops line both sides of Main on deep lots, with J. Jones's auto repair shop, a blacksmith and auto repair shop, a carpenter shop and a water tower near the middle of the sheet; St. John's Cemetery lies on the west side towards the south. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes with hydrants run along Main and High. The borough line crosses the east side of the sheet, and land beyond the drawn lots is marked vacant. The lower right of the sheet holds a separate inset of Nelsonville, which is not part of this reading. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Main is South Main Street; Yardville Road is Yardville-Allentown Road.
Placed from two junctions on Main (High and Yardville Road), one detected and one hand-picked; the helmert scale is 3.5 percent above the neighbouring sheets.
Allentown south-west: Main, High, Yardville Rd (part 1, turned, north to upper left); inset of Nelsonville at lower right (part 2, Road from Allentown and the Pemberton and Hightstown RR). 100 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Nelsonville (Road from Allentown at the Pemberton and Hightstown RR) (one rail crossing whose modern position is uncertain (Sharon Station Road or the abandoned line about 600 m east); north arrow and drawn road disagree by about 12 degrees; needs identify the old railroad line on the ground, then anchor on the crossing with px_per_ft 3.96).

sheet-5-1.description: The lower part of sheet 5, below a heavy rule, covers the centre of Allentown, Monmouth County, along Church from Pearl St. and Hamilton St. to Main, and Main south to the stone bridge over Doctor's Creek at Conine's Millpond. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. Church is lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, the Union A.M.E. church, the Grange hall and the fire department of the Hope Company, whose equipment is noted. Main holds the business centre: stores, offices and the First Baptist Church, with the Allentown Roller Mills of J. R. Conine and Son drawn beside the creek at the south end, together with a feed store and farm implement buildings on the east side. Water pipes of four and six inches with hydrants run along Church and Main. The part's northern edge is the dividing rule; the strip above it, which continues Church to the west as the road to Robbinsville, is a separate part of the sheet. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Main is North Main Street and South Main Street, divided at Church Street.
Placed from three points along Church (Pearl, Hamilton, Main), one hand-picked; a helmert along one street.

Allentown centre: Church, Pearl St., Hamilton St., Main to Doctor's Creek (part 1, below a heavy rule); strip above the rule continuing Church west as the Road to Robbinsville with the electric light plant (part 2). 100 ft.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: strip above the heavy rule: Church Street west to the Road to Robbinsville, Indian Run bridge, electric light plant and water works (no street junction drawn; needs step 6b: parcel corners or the Indian Run bridge on Church Street, with px_per_ft and north_deg from part 1).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the north part of the borough of Allentown, Monmouth County. Main runs north from Church to the borough limits at the top of the sheet, Broad crosses from Hamilton to Main, Pearl and Hamilton run north from Church and are joined by Mechanics, and Maiden Lane and Walker Av. leave Main to the east near Church. The sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. It shows the Methodist Episcopal church, Christ Church (Episcopal), St. John's Roman Catholic church, the Union A.M.E. parsonage, the public school, the Union Hotel, the Shore Road garage and Adam Spence's coal yard, with frame dwellings on the residential streets and two cemeteries, a large one west of Hamilton north of the Mechanics block and a smaller one east of Hamilton. Large areas north of Broad and west of Main are open land. Water pipes of four and six inches with hydrants run along Church, Main, Pearl and Hamilton. The borough limits are drawn as dash-dot lines on the east and north. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Modern names: Mechanics is Mechanic Street; Walker Avenue is Waker Street in OpenStreetMap; Main is North Main Street.
Allentown north: Main, Broad, Church, Pearl, Hamilton, Mechanics, Maiden Lane, Walker Av. 100 ft. One part.

sheet-7-1.description: The main part of sheet 7 covers the village of Imlaystown, Upper Freehold Township, Monmouth County. Main runs down the sheet from the junction of Allentown Road and Cox's Corner Road at the top, crossing Buckhole Creek by a stone bridge, to Red Valley Road, which leaves to the east, and continues south past Golden's Millpond. The village is a single row of frame dwellings, stores and shops along Main, with the Knights of Pythias hall, the Methodist Episcopal church, an auto repair shop, a pool room and Golden's grist mill, and further south the Upper Freehold Baptist Church and a public school. Mary B. Hendrickson's buildings stand east of Main and the Nelson Farm lies west of Allentown Road at the top left. Golden's Millpond and the creeks feeding it take up much of the lower half. A triangular inset at the top right, set off by heavy lines, shows more of Cox's Corner Road and is not part of this reading. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and dated January 1922; buildings are coloured by construction, yellow for frame, pink for brick, blue for stone, with dwellings marked D and outbuildings such as sheds, coops and auto garages drawn individually.
notes: Modern names: Main is Davis Station Road; Red Valley Road is Imlaystown Road; Allentown Road is Allentown-Lakewood Road; Cox's Corner Road is Imlaystown-Hightstown Road.

Anchored on one hand-picked junction (Main and Red Valley Road) with the scale of the neighbouring sheets and a rotation taken towards the top junction, which today is two road nodes 55 m apart: low confidence.
Imlaystown: Main, Allentown Rd, Cox's Corner Rd, Red Valley Rd, Golden's Millpond (part 1); triangular inset at top right with more of Cox's Corner Rd (part 2). 100 ft.
Not georeferenced on this sheet: inset: Cox's Corner Road north of Imlaystown (no street junction drawn; needs step 6b: parcel corners along Imlaystown-Hightstown Road).
